transcript:
[00:00] Alicia Park: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm alicia from redwood inference, i'm the AE on the partner motion. quick intros?
[00:08] Maya Chen: hi i'm maya, head of partnerships at altair, nice to meet you all. 
[00:12] Omar Haddad: omar here, vp eng, i'm responsible for infra and service ops.
[00:15] Ravi Menon: ravi, solutions eng at redwood, i'll drive the technical part.
[00:19] Diego Alvarez: diego, SE, i'll jump in on deployment questions.
[00:25] Jonas Rhee: jonas, tpm.
[00:30] Alicia Park: great, agenda — quick partner overview from redwood, then technical fit / pilot ideas, then commercial model and next steps. sound good?
[00:38] Maya Chen: sounds good. just to be clear, we're evaluating partners who can help us offer managed llm infra to our enterprise customers, so costs, slas and compliance are big for us.
[00:47] Alicia Park: understood — the short story: redwood's platform supports hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. we usually partner two ways — reseller/dedicated placement where partner runs the gpu infra and we provide the control plane and runtime, or a channel where you resell hosted api. both have different margin/time-to-value tradeoffs.
[01:10] Omar Haddad: question — for the dedicated model, how invasive is the control plane? we have strict networking and prefer a private control plane in a vpc or even on-prem for some customers.
[01:20] Ravi Menon: good question. redwood private supports a customer-managed control plane in a vpc and an on-prem package if needed. from infra side we need peering, outbound egress for telemetry (or you can opt out), and kms integration for keys. there's also an optional air-gapped package but that takes longer.
[01:36] Jonas Rhee: when you say kms integration, is that bring-your-own-kms (BYOK)? we need to map to our existing hsm provider.
[01:43] Diego Alvarez: yes BYOK is supported — we integrate with common KMS/HSM providers. it's a config + cert exchange flow, not code-level changes.
[01:51] Maya Chen: ok that helps. second, our customers care about per-token costs — how much of the runtime is optimized for quantized models and batching?
[02:01] Ravi Menon: redwood runtime selects quantization-friendly kernels and uses continuous batching and kv prefix caching to reduce per-token cost. typical gen workloads see 30-60% cost reduction vs naive single-token runs, depends on seq length and concurrency.
[02:18] Omar Haddad: you mentioned kv cache — can you explain how the cache is stored? is it server-side only, or can it be pinned to local instance memory?
[02:27] Ravi Menon: it's in-memory on the serving instance — we manage cache lifecycle. for private deployments you control instance sizes and we can expose cache configs so you can pin weights or caches to specific nodes.
[02:38] Maya Chen: any constraints re: gpu flavor? we run a mix of a100 and h100, and some customers want ampere next-gen.
[02:46] Diego Alvarez: redwood supports multiple GPU kernels; we do kernel selection at runtime. h100 gives best perf for large seqs but a100 is also supported. sometimes we recommend quantized fp4/INT8 paths for cost vs perf.
[02:58] Maya Chen: how invasive is the agent? like do you run a sidecar or full agent on host?
[03:03] Ravi Menon: it's a small runtime agent plus a control-plane connector. for private deploys it's typically containerized and orchestrated with k8s; for air-gapped we do a tarball + install script.
[03:15] Omar Haddad: latency SLAs — what can you guarantee?
[03:18] Alicia Park: for dedicated pools we offer SLA-backed latency targets, typical p95 numbers depend on model and batch profile. we'll need to run a pilot to define expected numbers for your workload shape.
[03:29] Maya Chen: pilot — how long, what do we provide?
[03:33] Ravi Menon: a 2-4 week bench test is common: you provide sample traces or synthetic traffic, we run parallel workloads on a small dedicated pool (or on your infra for private), collect tokens/sec, p50/p95 latencies, and cost estimates.
[03:45] Jonas Rhee: what's your telemetry/observability footprint? we need detailed audit logs for SOC2 and some customers want per-token traces for billing.
[03:54] Diego Alvarez: redwood console provides token-level cost and latency breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and audit logs. logs can be exported to your s3 or splunk, and we support syslog/elk integrations.
[04:10] Maya Chen: compliance — do you have SOC 2 / ISO and penetration testing artifacts?
[04:14] Alicia Park: yes SOC 2 type II and ISO certifications — we'll share the security pack, and we can do an NDA to exchange more detailed docs.
[04:21] Omar Haddad: commercial — reseller margins, price stack?
[04:25] Alicia Park: we typically do partner tiering — resale discount off hosted rates, or dedicated revenue share for committed capacity. margins depend on commit and volume. we'll share a partner program doc.
[04:36] Maya Chen: what about competitive differentiation — customers ask us why choose you over lambda/coreweave or just run vanilla k8s with open-source inference.
[04:46] Ravi Menon: our pitch is production-first: unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private, smart routing/fallbacks, and built-in cost controls (batching, cache, quantization) plus dev experience and observability. customers don't want to rebuild ops for each model.
[04:59] Omar Haddad: one thing — networking egress. some customers disallow any internet egress from their vpc. can redwood run without external egress?
[05:07] Diego Alvarez: yes, in air-gapped mode we can operate without external egress; for private vpc there's also an isolated mode where telemetry can be pushed to your collector without leaving the vpc.
[05:20] Maya Chen: timeline from our side: we have a few enterprise prospects asking for managed llm infra by end of q1 2027, so a pilot this quarter would be ideal.
[05:30] Alicia Park: ok good — propose we run a 2-week bench pilot on a small dedicated pool on altair infra or in redwood private in your vpc. rfe: alicia to send partner deck & pricing, ravi to propose bench runbook.
[05:45] Jonas Rhee: also want a short tech deep dive with our infra folks — maybe next week or the week after.
[05:52] Ravi Menon: we can do that — i'll send possible times.
[05:58] Maya Chen: thanks all, helpful.
[06:01] Alicia Park: thanks, quick recap of next steps and owners, we'll follow up with docs and schedule the tech session.
[06:09] (call ends)
